name: TX-14
label: Safe R

key_factors: Weber's large financial advantage ($920K vs. negative cash for Bartie)
Prediction markets price Weber at ~96% to win
No public polling in the race
model.rationale: Randy Weber holds a seat that leans Republican by double digits, has a commanding fundraising edge, and faces a Democratic challenger with essentially no money. Markets price this race as a near-certain Republican hold, and nothing in the evidence suggests otherwise.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic outside spending or unexpected polling showing a tighter race would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Republican incumbent Randy Weber is seeking another term in a southeast Texas district that leans Republican by about twelve points. He has raised nearly a million dollars and holds over $900,000 in cash, while Democratic challenger Thurman Bartie has raised under $30,000 and reports negative cash on hand. No outside groups are spending against Weber.

No public polls cover the race, and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive. Prediction markets give Weber roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. With the incumbent's structural, financial, and market advantages all aligned, the race sits firmly in the Republican-favored column, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
